en: to wind and surge; to roll in waves

examples.ko: 큰 강물이 굽이쳐 흐르는 모습을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the big river flowing in great curves.
The waves surged and rolled, so the boat rocked a lot.
The scenery of mountain ridges winding in sweeping curves is truly magnificent.
When the wind blew, the barley field rolled like waves.
The surging current gradually became calm.
I fished in a place where the water doesn't swirl and surge.

explain: '물결치다'와 비슷하지만 굽이치다는 강이나 산줄기, 큰 파도가 길고 크게 휘어지며 움직이는 느낌이 있어요. 주로 풍경을 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is similar to '물결치다' (to ripple), but 굽이치다 has the feel of rivers, mountain ridges or big waves moving in long, sweeping curves. It is mostly used when describing scenery.

examples.en: I sat and rested on a tree stump in the forest.

examples.ko: 나무를 베어 낸 자리에 그루터기만 남았어요.
examples.en: Only a stump was left where the tree had been cut.
A new sprout came up from the old stump.
A big stump sits there like a chair.
The kids climb up on the stump and play.

examples.ko: 그루터기의 나이테를 세어 보면 나무 나이를 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you count the rings on the stump, you can tell the tree's age.

explain: 나무나 풀을 베어 낸 뒤에 땅에 남은 부분을 말할 때 써요. 서 있는 나무의 아래쪽 줄기는 '밑동'이라고 해요.
explain_en: You use it for the part left in the ground after a tree or plant is cut down. The lower part of a tree that is still standing is called '밑동'.

examples.en: When spring came, the plum tree's buds burst open.

examples.ko: 꽃망울이 맺힌 걸 보니 곧 필 것 같아요.
examples.en: Seeing the buds form, they look like they'll bloom soon.

examples.ko: 아직 꽃망울만 있어서 벚꽃이 안 피었어요.
examples.en: There are only buds so far, so the cherry blossoms haven't bloomed.

examples.ko: 아침에 보니 꽃망울에 이슬이 맺혀 있어요.
examples.en: This morning I saw dew on the flower buds.
The little buds are opening one by one.

examples.ko: 장미 꽃망울은 아직 단단히 닫혀 있어요.
examples.en: The rose buds are still tightly closed.

explain: '꽃봉오리'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, 아직 피지 않았거나 막 피려는 꽃을 가리켜요. '꽃망울을 터뜨리다'는 꽃이 피기 시작한다는 말과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It can be used the same way as '꽃봉오리', and refers to a flower that has not opened yet or is about to. It goes well with '꽃망울을 터뜨리다', meaning a flower starts to bloom.

examples.en: In the old days, mules carried loads.
A mule is born from a horse and a donkey.
I saw an old man leading a mule on a country road.
A story about a mule and a farmer appears in the picture book.

examples.ko: 이 그림에는 노새 한 마리가 그려져 있어요.
examples.en: A mule is drawn in this picture.

examples.ko: 노새에 짐을 가득 싣고 길을 떠났어요.
examples.en: They loaded the mule with baggage and set off on the road.

explain: 당나귀와 헷갈리기 쉽지만 다른 동물이에요. 요즘은 직접 보기 어려워서 옛이야기나 그림, 책에서 주로 만나요.
explain_en: It is easy to mix up with a donkey, but it is a different animal. Today it is hard to see in person, so you mostly meet it in old tales, pictures and books.

examples.en: Sharp thorns have grown on the rose stem.

examples.ko: 아기 새 등에 날개가 돋치기 시작했어요.
examples.en: Wings have started to grow on the baby bird's back.

examples.ko: 그 말에 가시가 돋쳐 있어서 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: That remark had thorns in it, and it hurt me.
The new product is selling like hotcakes.

examples.ko: 가시 돋친 말은 하지 않는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better not to say cutting words.

examples.ko: 그 선인장은 줄기마다 뾰족한 가시가 돋쳐 있어요.
examples.en: That cactus has pointy spines growing on every stem.

explain: 가시나 날개 같은 것이 몸에서 뾰족하게 나올 때 써요. 새싹이나 소름, 여드름이 나올 때는 보통 '돋다', '돋아나다'를 써요. 실제 대화에서는 '날개 돋친 듯', '가시 돋친'처럼 굳은 표현으로 가장 많이 만나요.

phrases.example: 새로 나온 과자가 날개 돋친 듯 팔리고 있어요.
phrases.en: The newly released snack is selling like hotcakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상품이 아주 빠르게 많이 팔릴 때 쓰는 관용 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An idiom for a product selling very quickly in large numbers.

phrases.example: 화가 났다고 가시 돋친 말을 하면 후회해요.
phrases.en: If you say cutting words out of anger, you'll regret it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대를 아프게 찌르는 듯한 비꼬는 말을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to sharp, sarcastic words that sting the other person.

explain_en: It is used when things like thorns or wings grow sharply out of a body. For sprouts, goosebumps or pimples, people usually say '돋다' or '돋아나다'. In real conversation you'll most often meet it in fixed expressions like '날개 돋친 듯' and '가시 돋친'.

examples.ko: 창가에 커튼 그림자가 길게 드리워져 있어요.
examples.en: The curtain's shadow stretches long by the window.

examples.ko: 해가 지면서 산 그림자가 마을에 드리워졌어요.
examples.en: As the sun set, the mountain's shadow fell over the village.
A look of tiredness hung over his face.
A cool shade was cast beneath the tree.

examples.ko: 겨울 아침, 골목에 짙은 안개가 드리워져 있었어요.
examples.en: On the winter morning, thick fog hung over the alley.
Moonlight softly fell across the lake.

explain: 그림자, 그늘, 안개, 커튼처럼 위에서 아래로 늘어지거나 넓게 깔리는 것에 써요. '그림자가 드리워지다'가 가장 자주 나오고, 나쁜 일의 조짐이라는 비유로도 써요. 하는 쪽은 '드리우다'예요.

phrases.example: 그 소식 이후 회사에 어두운 그림자가 드리워졌어요.
phrases.en: A dark shadow falls over something.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 나쁜 일이 생길 것 같은 불안한 분위기가 퍼진다는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for an uneasy mood spreading, as if something bad is about to happen.

explain_en: It is used for things that hang down or spread wide, such as shadows, shade, fog and curtains. '그림자가 드리워지다' is the most common phrase, and it is also used figuratively for signs of bad things. The active verb is '드리우다'.

examples.en: I waited for a whole hour under the scorching sun.
I walked in the blazing midday sun and now I feel dizzy.
There was no one on the playground where the sun beat down.
The farmers kept working in the fields even in the scorching sun.
I went into the shade of a tree to avoid the blazing sun.

examples.ko: 오늘은 땡볕이라 모자를 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: The sun is scorching today, so you must wear a hat.

explain: 여름에 아주 뜨겁게 내리쬐는 햇볕을 말해요. 그냥 '햇볕'이나 '뜨거운 햇볕'보다 구어에서 더 생생하고 힘든 느낌이 있어요. '땡볕 아래', '땡볕에서'처럼 그 안에서 고생하는 상황과 자주 같이 나와요.
explain_en: It describes the sun beating down fiercely in summer. Compared with plain '햇볕' (sunlight), it sounds more vivid and conveys hardship in spoken Korean. It often appears in phrases like '땡볕 아래' and '땡볕에서' describing someone struggling in it.

en: to surge; to move in waves; to roll

examples.en: When the wind blew, the barley field rippled like waves.
The lake is gently rippling.
The flags of the cheering crowd wave like a sea.
I looked at the sea, rolling with waves, for a long time.
Her long hair flowed in the wind, and it looked pretty.
The cheers of the people will surge through the square.

explain: 실제 물뿐 아니라 밀밭, 머리카락, 깃발, 사람들의 감정이 파도처럼 이어서 움직이는 모습에도 써요. 말할 때보다 글이나 묘사에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is used for real water but also for wheat fields, hair, flags and people's emotions moving in a wave-like way. You see it more in writing and description than in everyday speech.

examples.en: White clouds billowed up in the sky.
Smoke is rising in billows from the chimney.

examples.ko: 뭉게뭉게 떠 있는 구름을 보며 누워 있었어요.
examples.en: I lay there watching the puffy clouds floating by.
I made a soup with steam billowing off it.
Clouds gather in puffs in the autumn sky.
I can see smoke pouring out of the factory in billows.

explain: 구름, 연기, 김이 둥글고 크게 계속 피어오르는 모습에 써요. '피어오르다, 올라가다, 나다' 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 같은 뿌리의 '뭉게구름'은 뭉게뭉게 떠 있는 구름이에요.
explain_en: It describes clouds, smoke or steam rising in big round puffs, one after another. It goes well with verbs like '피어오르다', '올라가다' and '나다'. The related word '뭉게구름' is a puffy cloud.

examples.en: A gentle breeze comes through the window, so it's cool.
The flag sways gently in the breeze.
I walked through the park in the spring breeze.
A breeze blows in from the sea and I feel good.

examples.ko: 미풍 덕분에 더운 날씨도 견딜 만했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the breeze, even the hot weather was bearable.

examples.ko: 건물 양쪽 깃대의 깃발이 미풍을 받아 조용히 펄럭여요.
examples.en: The flags on both sides of the building flutter quietly in the breeze.

explain: '산들바람', '실바람'과 비슷하게 약하고 부드러운 바람이에요. '미풍'은 한자어라서 글이나 방송에서 더 자연스럽고, 일상에서는 '바람이 살살 불다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is a weak, soft wind like '산들바람' or '실바람'. Because it is a Sino-Korean word, it sounds more natural in writing and broadcasts; in daily talk people say '바람이 살살 불다'.

en: with a twinkle; in a flash

examples.en: A star twinkled in the night sky.
A good idea suddenly flashed into my mind.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣자 아이의 눈이 반짝 빛났어요.
examples.en: The child's eyes lit up when he heard that.

examples.ko: 멀리서 등대 불빛이 반짝 하고 보였어요.
examples.en: A lighthouse light flickered into view in the distance.

examples.ko: 전등이 반짝 하고 켜졌다가 바로 꺼졌어요.
examples.en: The light blinked on and went right off again.

examples.ko: 반짝 추위가 와서 두꺼운 옷을 꺼냈어요.
examples.en: A short cold snap came, so I took out thick clothes.

explain: '반짝'은 한 번 빛나는 모습이고, '반짝반짝'은 계속 빛나거나 깨끗하게 빛나는 모습이에요. 번개처럼 더 강한 빛은 '번쩍'이 어울려요. 시간이 짧게 지나간다는 뜻으로 '반짝 추위', '반짝 세일'처럼도 써요.

phrases.example: 그 노래는 반짝 인기를 끌다가 곧 잊혔어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠깐 크게 유행했다가 금방 사라지는 인기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Popularity that surges briefly and fades quickly.
phrases.en_equiv: flash in the pan; short-lived fame

explain_en: 반짝 is a single flash, while 반짝반짝 is continuous sparkling or shiny clean. A stronger light such as lightning fits 번쩍. It also marks something brief, as in 반짝 추위 (short cold snap) and 반짝 세일 (flash sale).

examples.ko: 여름에 북유럽에 가면 백야를 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you go to Northern Europe in summer, you can see the white nights.

examples.ko: 백야 때문에 밤 열 시에도 하늘이 환해요.
examples.en: Because of the white nights, the sky is still bright even at ten at night.

examples.ko: 백야 기간에는 잠을 자기가 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: During the white night period, it isn't easy to sleep.
I traveled in Finland during the white night season.

examples.ko: 백야가 시작되면 사람들이 밤늦게까지 밖에 있어요.
examples.en: When the white nights begin, people stay outside until late at night.

examples.ko: 백야를 처음 겪은 친구는 밤새 잠을 설쳤어요.
examples.en: My friend, who was experiencing the white nights for the first time, barely slept all night.

explain: 여름에 북극이나 남극에 가까운 지역에서 볼 수 있는 현상이라서 '북유럽의 백야'처럼 지역과 함께 자주 나와요. 반대로 겨울에 해가 거의 뜨지 않는 현상은 '극야'라고 해요.
explain_en: It happens in summer in regions close to the Arctic or Antarctic, so it often appears with place names, as in 'the white nights of Northern Europe'. The opposite, when the sun barely rises in winter, is called '극야'.

examples.en: It has been drizzling since morning.

examples.ko: 부슬부슬 내리는 비 속을 천천히 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked slowly through the drizzling rain.

examples.ko: 가을 오후에 부슬부슬 비가 와서 기분이 차분해요.
examples.en: A light rain on an autumn afternoon makes me feel calm.

examples.ko: 부슬부슬 내리는 비라서 우산 없이 나왔어요.
examples.en: It was only a light drizzle, so I came out without an umbrella.

examples.ko: 부슬부슬 비가 오는 날에는 전이 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: On days when it drizzles, I want to eat jeon.
The drizzle that had been falling stopped in the evening.

explain: 가늘고 조용하게 내리는 비를 말할 때 써요. 센 비는 '주룩주룩'처럼 다른 말을 써요. '보슬보슬'도 비슷한데 더 부드럽고 작은 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes thin, quiet rain. Heavy rain is described with other words such as '주룩주룩'. '보슬보슬' is similar but feels even softer and finer.

examples.en: A light drizzle has been falling since morning.

examples.ko: 부슬비 오는 날에는 우산 없이 걷기도 해요.
examples.en: On drizzly days I sometimes walk without an umbrella.
I walked slowly in the drizzle.
It's just a drizzle, so it's fine without an umbrella.
The drizzle stopped when evening came.

examples.ko: 가을 부슬비 소리를 들으면 마음이 편해져요.
examples.en: Listening to the autumn drizzle makes me feel calm.

explain: 가늘고 조용하게 내리는 비예요. '이슬비', '보슬비'와 비슷하고, 갑자기 세게 오는 '소나기'와는 느낌이 반대예요.
explain_en: It is rain that falls thinly and quietly. It is similar to '이슬비' and '보슬비', and feels the opposite of a sudden heavy '소나기' shower.

examples.en: A typhoon suddenly struck last night.
A cold wave will hit this winter.
The wind of redevelopment has swept into our neighborhood too.
We all got through the crisis that struck us together.

examples.ko: 비바람이 불어닥치기 전에 창문을 단단히 닫아 두세요.
examples.en: Close the windows tightly before the wind and rain hit.
With a job crunch hitting, graduates are very worried.

explain: 세고 갑작스러운 바람이나 한파, 태풍에 써요. 불경기, 위기, 유행 같은 큰 흐름이 갑자기 닥칠 때도 쓰고, '변화의 바람이 불어닥치다'처럼 비유로 많이 나와요. 부드러운 바람에도 쓰는 '불어오다'보다 훨씬 거센 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used for strong, sudden wind, cold waves and typhoons. It also describes big trends such as a recession, a crisis or a fad hitting suddenly, often figuratively as in '변화의 바람이 불어닥치다'. It feels much fiercer than '불어오다', which can describe even a gentle breeze.

examples.ko: 저녁이 되니 바깥은 어두워졌지만 굵은 빗발이 유리창을 세차게 때려요.
examples.en: It got dark outside by evening, but thick streaks of rain still pound the window.
The rain gradually thinned out.
I ran to school through the pouring rain.
My umbrella flipped inside out in the driving rain.

examples.ko: 굵은 빗발 속에서도 아이들은 신나게 놀아요.
examples.en: The kids play happily even in the heavy rain.

examples.ko: 빗발이 약해지면 그때 출발하는 게 좋겠어요.
examples.en: It would be better to set off once the rain weakens.

explain: '비'가 내리는 물 전체를 가리키는 것과 달리, '빗발'은 줄기처럼 쏟아지는 모양을 가리켜요. '빗줄기'와 거의 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. '빗발이 굵다', '빗발이 가늘어지다', '빗발이 세다'처럼 굵기와 세기를 말할 때 어울려요. '빗발치다'에도 이 말이 들어 있어요.
explain_en: Unlike '비', which refers to rain as a whole, '빗발' refers to rain falling in streaks. It can almost always be swapped with '빗줄기'. It suits talk about thickness and strength, as in '빗발이 굵다', '빗발이 가늘어지다' and '빗발이 세다'. The word also appears inside '빗발치다'.

examples.en: The plane slowly circled above the city.
The sea looked really wide from high up in the sky.

examples.ko: 오늘 아침 서울 상공에 짙은 안개가 꼈어요.
examples.en: Thick fog hung over Seoul this morning.

examples.ko: 구름 위 상공은 공기가 차고 얇아요.
examples.en: The sky high above the clouds is cold and thin.
The drone went up to fifty meters in the air.
Because of the smoke, the sky above looked hazy.

explain: 어떤 장소의 위쪽 하늘을 말할 때 써요. '서울 상공'처럼 땅 이름과 함께 쓰는 말이에요. 그냥 '하늘'은 어디에나 쓰지만 상공은 뉴스나 안내 방송에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: Use it for the sky above a specific place, usually with a place name, as in '서울 상공'. 하늘 works anywhere, while 상공 is often heard in news and announcements.

en: to make crisp sounds; to rustle

examples.ko: 눈길을 걸을 때마다 신발 밑에서 눈이 서걱거려요.
examples.en: Every time I walk on the snowy path, the snow crunches under my shoes.

examples.ko: 갈대밭을 지나자 마른 갈대가 서걱거리는 소리가 들렸어요.
examples.en: As I passed the reed field, I heard the dry reeds rustling.

examples.ko: 모래가 들어갔는지 밥을 씹을 때 입안에서 서걱거렸어요.
examples.en: There must have been sand in it, because it grated in my mouth when I chewed the rice.

examples.ko: 빙수 얼음이 서걱거려서 먹는 재미가 있어요.
examples.en: The shaved ice crunches, which makes it fun to eat.

examples.ko: 발밑에서 서걱거리던 눈 소리가 멈추고 곧 조용해졌어요.
examples.en: The crunching of snow under my feet stopped, and it soon grew quiet.

examples.ko: 서걱거릴 정도로 마른 볏짚 위에 누웠어요.
examples.en: I lay down on rice straw so dry that it rustled.

explain: 눈, 모래, 갈대, 마른 풀처럼 알갱이나 결이 거친 것이 스치거나 밟힐 때 나는 소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요. '서걱서걱'은 소리 자체이고 '서걱거리다'는 그 소리가 계속 난다는 동사예요. 말보다 글에서 더 자주 만나요.
explain_en: It imitates the sound made when something gritty or coarse, like snow, sand, reeds or dry grass, rubs or is stepped on. '서걱서걱' is the sound itself, and '서걱거리다' is the verb meaning that sound keeps going. You meet it more in writing than in speech.

examples.ko: 창밖에는 끝없이 하얀 설원이 펼쳐져 있었어요.
examples.en: Outside the window, an endless white snowfield stretched out.

examples.ko: 스키어들이 눈 덮인 설원을 가로지르며 달렸어요.
examples.en: The skiers raced across the snow-covered field.
On my winter trip, I saw a snowfield for the first time.

examples.ko: 설원 위에서 사슴 한 마리가 먹이를 찾고 있었어요.
examples.en: A deer was looking for food on the snowfield.
I saw the aurora over a snowfield in a northern country.

examples.ko: 설원을 걷다 보니 발자국만 길게 남았어요.
examples.en: As I walked across the snowfield, only a long line of footprints remained.

explain: 넓게 눈이 덮인 벌판을 말해요. 여행이나 사진, 풍경을 그릴 때 어울리는 조금 멋진 표현이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '눈밭'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to a wide field covered in snow. It is a slightly poetic word that suits travel, photos and scenery descriptions. In everyday talk people also say '눈밭'.

examples.ko: 어항에 수초를 넣어서 물고기가 숨을 곳을 만들었어요.
examples.en: I put water plants in the fish tank to make a hiding place for the fish.
Lots of water plants grow in this pond.
My fishing line keeps getting caught on the water plants.
The fish eggs are stuck to the water plants.
To grow water plants, there has to be enough light.

examples.ko: 수초가 물을 깨끗하게 만드는 데 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Water plants help keep the water clean.

explain: 물속이나 물가에서 자라는 풀을 말하고, 특히 어항이나 연못, 낚시 이야기에서 많이 나와요. 쉬운 말로는 '물풀'이라고도 해요. 과학 시간에는 '수생식물'이라는 말도 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to plants growing in water or at the water's edge, and it comes up often in talk about aquariums, ponds and fishing. A plainer word is '물풀'. In science class you may also meet '수생식물'.

examples.en: A fair wind blew, and the boat moved quickly.

examples.ko: 오늘은 순풍 덕분에 자전거 타기가 힘들지 않았어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the tailwind, cycling wasn't hard today.
The yacht runs across the sea on a fair wind.

examples.ko: 처음엔 순풍이 불더니 갑자기 바람이 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: At first there was a fair wind, but suddenly the wind changed.

examples.ko: 뒤에서 순풍이 불어 줘서 걷기 편했어요.
examples.en: A tailwind was blowing from behind, so walking was comfortable.

examples.ko: 이 항구는 순풍이 부는 날에 배가 많이 떠나요.
examples.en: Many ships leave this port on days with a fair wind.

explain: 가려는 방향으로, 뒤에서 불어 주는 바람이에요. 반대말은 '역풍'이고, 일이 잘 풀릴 때 비유로도 써요.

phrases.example: 새 가게가 순풍에 돛 단 듯 잘되고 있어요.
phrases.en: The new shop is doing well, like a ship with its sails up in a fair wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 막힘없이 아주 잘 풀릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when things go very smoothly without any obstacles.

explain_en: It is a wind that blows from behind, in the direction you are going. Its opposite is '역풍', and it is also used figuratively when things go well.

en: to be bleak; to be chilly

examples.en: The autumn wind is blowing, so the street feels bleak.

examples.ko: 밤이 되자 빈집 주변이 스산한 분위기로 변했어요.
examples.en: When night fell, the area around the empty house took on an eerie, desolate mood.

examples.ko: 스산하게 비가 내리는 날에는 따뜻한 차가 생각나요.
examples.en: On days when the rain falls chilly and gloomy, I think of hot tea.

examples.ko: 낙엽이 다 떨어지니 공원이 스산해 보여요.
examples.en: Now that all the leaves have fallen, the park looks bleak.

examples.ko: 마음이 스산해서 오늘은 일찍 집에 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: I felt kind of empty inside, so I came home early today.

examples.ko: 영화 속 숲은 안개가 껴서 더 스산했어요.
examples.en: The forest in the movie was even eerier because of the fog.

explain: 쌀쌀한 날씨와 쓸쓸하고 으스스한 분위기를 함께 느낄 때 써요. '쌀쌀하다'는 주로 기온 이야기이고, 스산하다는 풍경이나 마음의 쓸쓸함까지 담아요. 가을, 겨울, 빈집, 밤거리와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Use it when chilly weather and a lonely, slightly eerie mood come together. '쌀쌀하다' is mostly about temperature, while 스산하다 also covers the desolate feel of a scene or of your heart. It fits autumn, winter, empty houses and night streets.

en: to be sunny; to be sunlit

examples.ko: 우리 집 마당은 하루 종일 양지발라요.
examples.en: Our yard is sunny all day long.

examples.ko: 할머니는 양지바른 마루에 앉아 졸고 계세요.
examples.en: Grandmother is dozing on the sunny porch.

examples.ko: 양지바르고 조용한 동네로 이사 가고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to move to a sunny, quiet neighborhood.
This room gets a lot of sun, so it's warm even in winter.
If the house is sunny, the potted plants grow well.

examples.ko: 고양이가 양지바른 담 밑에서 자고 있어요.
examples.en: The cat is sleeping under the sunny wall.

explain: '양지바른 곳', '양지바른 마당'처럼 꾸미는 말로 가장 많이 써요. 반대는 해가 안 드는 '음지'예요. '바르다'가 르 불규칙이라 '양지발라요'가 돼요.
explain_en: It is most often used to modify a noun, as in '양지바른 곳' or '양지바른 마당'. The opposite place is the shady '음지'. Because '바르다' is a 르-irregular verb, it becomes '양지발라요'.

en: to be dim; to be fairly dark

examples.ko: 겨울에는 다섯 시만 되어도 밖이 어둑어둑해요.
examples.en: In winter, it's already dim outside at five o'clock.
As soon as I entered the dim forest, I suddenly got scared.
We played in the park until it got dim.

examples.ko: 저녁 무렵 집 안이 어둑해서 불을 켰어요.
examples.en: It got dim inside the house in the evening, so I turned on the lights.
It's dim outside, so be careful on your way.

examples.ko: 어둑어둑한 골목길을 혼자 걸으려니 조금 무서웠어요.
examples.en: Walking alone down the dim alley was a little scary.

explain: 완전히 깜깜하지는 않고 해 질 무렵이나 새벽처럼 조금 어두운 때에 써요. '어둑어둑하다'처럼 반복해서 말하면 서서히 어두워지는 느낌이 살아나요.
explain_en: It is used for mild darkness, like dusk or early dawn, when it isn't fully dark. Repeating it as '어둑어둑하다' brings out the feeling of slowly getting darker.

examples.en: The dawn sky is faintly getting light.
The building looked dim through the fog.
I vaguely remember things from my childhood.
Moonlight comes faintly into the room.
That person's face comes back to me dimly.

examples.ko: 저녁 무렵 골목에 불빛이 어슴푸레 켜졌어요.
examples.en: Toward evening, lights came on dimly in the alley.

explain: '희미하게'와 비슷하지만 '어슴푸레'는 새벽이나 저녁처럼 어둑한 빛 속에서 흐릿하게 보이는 분위기가 강해요. 기억이 흐릿할 때도 쓸 수 있어요. 비슷한 말로 '어스름'이 있어요.
explain_en: It is similar to '희미하게' (faintly), but '어슴푸레' carries a stronger feeling of things looking blurry in dim light, like dawn or dusk. You can also use it for a hazy memory. A related word is '어스름'.

examples.en: Lotus flowers have bloomed fully in the pond.
I want to go to the lotus festival in summer.

examples.ko: 연꽃은 진흙 속에서 자라지만 깨끗해 보여요.
examples.en: A lotus grows in mud but looks clean.

examples.ko: 절 마당에 연꽃 등이 걸려 있었어요.
examples.en: Lotus lanterns were hanging in the temple yard.

examples.ko: 그림 속 연꽃이 아주 곱게 그려졌어요.
examples.en: The lotus flower in the painting is drawn very delicately.
My friend sent me a photo of lotus flowers.

explain: '연꽃'은 불교와 관련이 깊어서 절에서 자주 보이는 꽃이에요. 식물은 '연', 잎은 '연잎'이라고 해서 음식 '연잎밥'에도 이 말이 들어가요.
explain_en: 연꽃 is closely tied to Buddhism and is often seen at temples. The plant is 연 and its leaf is 연잎, which is also why the dish 연잎밥 has this word in it.

examples.en: Thunder is rumbling among the dark clouds.
The sky rumbled, and soon a shower fell.
The machines at the construction site rumbled all day.

examples.ko: 멀리서 우르릉거리는 소리가 들려서 창문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: I heard a rumbling sound far away, so I closed the window.
It looks like thunder will rumble from the evening.
A truck rumbled through the alley.

explain: 주로 천둥, 큰 차, 기계 소리에 써요. 사람 배에서 나는 소리는 '꾸르륵'이라고 해요. '우르릉대다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for thunder, big vehicles and machines. A rumbling stomach is '꾸르륵' instead. '우르릉대다' is used with the same meaning.

examples.en: This city has many canals.
Boats move slowly along the canal.

examples.ko: 파나마 운하는 두 바다를 이어 줘요.
examples.en: The Panama Canal connects two oceans.
I walked along the path beside the canal.
People in the past carried goods by canal.
The water in the canal has become clean.

explain: 자연에 있는 물길은 '강'이나 '개천'이라고 하고, 배가 다니거나 물을 보내려고 사람이 판 물길만 운하라고 해요. '파나마 운하', '수에즈 운하'처럼 이름 뒤에 붙여요.
explain_en: A waterway that occurs in nature is called 강 or 개천. Only a channel dug by people for ships or for moving water is called 운하. It follows the name, as in 파나마 운하 and 수에즈 운하.

examples.ko: 호수 위에 백조가 유유히 떠 있어요.
examples.en: A swan is floating leisurely on the lake.

examples.ko: 그는 급한 일이 없다는 듯 유유하게 걸어요.
examples.en: He walks calmly, as if he has nothing urgent to do.

examples.ko: 유유한 강물을 보고 있으면 마음이 편해요.
examples.en: Watching the slowly flowing river makes my mind feel at ease.
That person always looks so unhurried that I envy them.
I spent a calm and relaxed day.
Being unhurried does not mean being lazy.

explain: 거의 '유유히'의 꼴로 많이 써요. 강물, 구름, 걸음처럼 급하지 않고 여유 있는 모습에 쓰고, 급한 상황에서 태연한 모습에도 써요. '유유히 사라지다'가 자주 나오는 표현이에요. 비슷한 말로 '느긋하다', '여유롭다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is most often used in the form '유유히'. It describes an unhurried, easygoing manner, such as flowing water, clouds or a walk, and also a calm look in an urgent situation. '유유히 사라지다' (to slip away calmly) is a common expression. Similar words are '느긋하다' and '여유롭다'.

examples.en: I went to see a yellow canola flower field on Jeju Island.
In spring, canola blooms all along the roadside.
Oil is pressed from canola seeds and used in cooking.

examples.ko: 유채는 이른 봄부터 노란 꽃이 펴요.
examples.en: Canola produces yellow flowers from early spring.
Many people take photos in the canola field.
This restaurant's canola greens side dish is tasty.

explain: 유채는 봄에 노란 꽃이 피는 식물이라서 제주도 하면 가장 먼저 떠오르는 꽃 중 하나예요. 씨로는 기름을 짜고, 어린 잎은 나물로 먹기도 해요. 같은 노란 봄꽃인 '개나리'는 나무이고 유채는 풀이라 달라요.
explain_en: 유채 is a plant with yellow spring flowers and is one of the first flowers people think of with Jeju. Its seeds are pressed for oil and its young leaves are eaten as a seasoned vegetable. 개나리, another yellow spring flower, is a shrub, while 유채 is an herbaceous plant.
